Donald Trump yearned for a ceasefire deal. When it came, it was a losing deal
for him, underscoring how [desperate](https://zeteo.com/p/the-new-iran-peace-
deal-is-a-humiliation) he was to get out of his self-made problem. He
swallowed it. And things were beginning to alleviate. Oil prices started to go
down. But now, mere weeks later, not only has the ceasefire collapsed but the
[Mad King](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-one-year-america-first-mad-king) is
drastically ratcheting up his disastrous war once again.

And Trump is doing so as the global economy runs dangerously close to going
off the cliff. U.S. oil reserves are at the [lowest
level](https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/crude-
oil/071526-us-strategic-oil-reserve-falls-to-lowest-level-since-1983) _since
1983._ And while global reserves helped stave off higher price increases
previously, those reserves have [now been
tapped](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-07-15/oil-reserves-spent-imf-us-iran-
war/106918074); there is less and less to draw from as the highly unnecessary
crisis gets increasingly worse.

And as Trumpland _apparently_ tries to restart negotiations - while
threatening more drastic violence - Iran is expressing little interest. To
make matters worse, the Houthis are moving to close the [Bab-al-Mandeb Strait
](https://zeteo.com/p/7-things-you-need-to-know-about-the-bde)to Saudi
tankers. The blockade would [hinder](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/middle-
east/yemen-houthis-maritime-embargo-saudi-arabia-oil-rcna588345) an additional
7% of global oil supply - almost doubling the oil currently reduced by the
Iranian blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

All the while, Ukraine has
[dismantled](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/ukraine-cripples-
russian-refining-global-230000948.html) Russia's refinery capacity. All to
say, the likelihood of global oil shortages has spiked.

This was supposed to be over.
